findings.claim: The new 'get' category grants the 8 locator actions, each of which dispatches click/fill/check/hover subactions, so the docs' restrictive policy permits arbitrary form fills and clicks it explicitly denies.
findings.evidence: Built the branch and ran it: with the docs policy verbatim, 'fill #s pwned' was denied, 'find label Secret fill pwned' returned Done, and 'get value #s' returned 'pwned'. FIND_ACTIONS at cli/src/native/actions.rs:8049 = click,fill,check,hover,text; all 8 FIND_SUBACTION_COMMANDS are in the get category.

findings.claim: The 'wait' category includes waitforfunction, which Runtime.evaluates a caller-supplied expression, so deny:['eval'] does not remove script execution and the docs' restrictive allow-list grants it.
findings.evidence: With {default:allow, deny:[eval]}: 'eval' denied, 'wait --fn "(()=>{document.title=...})()"' ran and the title changed. With the docs restrictive policy the same expression read #s and returned its value into agent output.

findings.claim: removeinitscript is in no category, so deny:['eval'] does not gate removal of the init script that installs the WebSocket/EventSource override the docs point at.
findings.evidence: network.rs:174 installs the override via Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument; handle_removeinitscript (actions.rs:7110) forwards any caller-supplied identifier to Page.removeScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument; policy probe confirms check('removeinitscript') == Allow under deny:[eval].
findings.layer: policy unit probe plus call-path read; a working end-to-end removal of the allowlist script was not demonstrated

findings.claim: The 'state' category covers only 4 actions; the destructive and secret-reading state surface (state_clear, state_clean, state_rename, cookies_clear, cookies_get, storage_clear, storage_get, credentials, credentials_set, clipboard, headers, dialog) is uncategorized and passes a deny:['state'] policy.
findings.evidence: Policy probe asserted Allow for all 12 under {default:allow, deny:[state,fill,click]}; 'state list' ran successfully end-to-end under that policy.
findings.layer: policy unit probe plus end-to-end CLI

findings.claim: Text entry and clicking survive deny:['fill','click'] via the interact category (keydown/keyup, mouse down/up) and the uncategorized inserttext; the fill/interact split puts equivalent capabilities on opposite sides of the boundary.
findings.evidence: End-to-end: 'click button' denied while 'mouse move/down/up' all returned Done under {deny:[click,fill,...]}. Probe asserted Allow for keydown and inserttext.
findings.layer: end-to-end CLI plus policy unit probe

findings.claim: pushstate mutates the document URL and is in no category, so deny:['navigate'] does not gate it.
findings.evidence: End-to-end: 'open file:///...' denied with action 'navigate', 'pushstate /injected' passed the policy gate (failed later on a page JS error, not on policy).

findings.claim: 11 of the 83 table entries are unreachable from the CLI and from MCP, including 6 of the 7 eval members the issue names as the security motivation.
findings.evidence: parse_command_inner has no passthrough arm (commands.rs:2016 returns UnknownCommand); no parser arm or output.rs help entry emits addscript, addinitscript, addstyle, expose, setcontent, evalhandle, multiselect, selectall, setvalue, clear, dispatch. MCP builds CLI argv via call_cli_tool, so it inherits the parser's surface. --init-script rides on the launch command as an initScripts field (main.rs:86), not as an addinitscript action.
findings.layer: static enumeration of parser arms and MCP tool construction

findings.claim: The docs edit introduces a claim the code does not implement: the state row now says 'set credentials', but no credentials action is in the state category.
findings.evidence: docs/src/app/security/page.mdx:255 vs cli/src/native/policy.rs:110-113; policy probe shows check('credentials') and check('credentials_set') both Allow under deny:[state].
findings.layer: diff read plus policy unit probe

findings.claim: Nothing pins the docs table, the code table, and the real action set to each other, so the drift this PR fixes can silently recur.
findings.evidence: The new test_docs_restrictive_policy_allows_repro_actions hardcodes a 15-name list rather than deriving it; no test relates ACTION_CATEGORIES to DOCUMENTED_ACTIONS or to the dispatch match; the mdx is not parsed by any test.

exemptions.claim: Precedence is correct: category deny beats category and exact allow; exact names stay narrow.
exemptions.evidence: check() evaluates deny before confirm before allow (policy.rs:205-241); action_matches only expands an entry that is itself a category name, so deny:['evalhandle'] leaves 'evaluate' allowed. The author's own tests cover both and pass.

policy_actions_for_command (actions.rs:2073) returns concrete action names plus plugin actions of the form plugin:<name>:<capability>; colons cannot equal a category name and appear in no table entry, so those fall through to exact equality. The loop at actions.rs:2213 checks every element and denies on the first Deny.

exemptions.claim: Confirmation cannot leak across a category.
exemptions.evidence: handle_confirm (actions.rs:10648) inserts only pending.action, and the gate is an exact HashSet::contains at actions.rs:2223 and 2253, so approving evalhandle does not satisfy evaluate. Approval is also scoped to the replayed command and restored afterwards (10657).

exemptions.claim: requires_confirmation did not diverge from check.
exemptions.evidence: Both call the same action_matches; the author's test_each_category_resolves_to_all_members asserts them together over the whole table.

exemptions.claim: Uncategorized actions are fail-closed under a default:deny allow-list.
exemptions.evidence: check() returns Deny for any action absent from a non-empty allow list when default is deny (policy.rs:225); verified end-to-end when 'fill' and 'click' were denied under the docs policy.
One comment line; the stale action-policy.ts reference is gone and no code path reads it.

issue_candidates.title: DOCUMENTED_ACTIONS omits cdp_url
issue_candidates.evidence: cli/src/commands.rs:2529 emits action cdp_url and actions.rs dispatches it, but it is absent from DOCUMENTED_ACTIONS in cli/src/native/parity_tests.rs:45-190.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Pre-existing gap in the parity list; the diff neither created nor touched it.

issue_candidates.title: The daemon socket accepts raw JSON commands, so action policy is advisory against any caller with shell access
issue_candidates.evidence: cli/src/native/daemon.rs:530-556 deserializes an arbitrary line into a command and calls execute_command; the policy gate is inside execute_command but the socket has no caller authentication.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Architectural property of the daemon, unrelated to categorization. Worth stating in the Known limitations section.

issue_candidates.title: deny:['click'] is bypassable via mouse down/up regardless of categories
issue_candidates.evidence: Exact matching had the same hole; mousedown and mouseup are distinct actions that synthesize a click.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Pre-existing under exact matching; listed as F5 only because the diff turns interact into a grantable category.

issue_candidates.title: `wait` silently swallows unknown flags instead of erroring
issue_candidates.evidence: `agent-browser wait --function "expr"` matched no flag branch in the wait arm (cli/src/commands.rs:690-760) and fell through to the selector path, hanging 25s and reporting 'Wait timed out' rather than naming the unknown flag. The correct flag is --fn.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Parser ergonomics unrelated to policy categories; found while probing waitforfunction.
